## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c9d08f393617e7f46b9e346537fbb8b8ebd681c7`
Local-runs: probe — `node scripts/pm/label-write.mjs --self-test`, run in a throwaway worktree of the head (`/tmp/claude-0/seat3/wt-31250`, since removed), because the brief asks for the head's own counts (exit 0; 163 cases across 13 batteries). In a throwaway worktree of `origin/main` (also removed) the same command gave 144 across 12. In the head worktree I also ran: the mutation (both `refuseKindLabels` call sites set to `null`, then restored: 10 of 163 fail, exactly the ten the thread names); `close-cards.mjs --self-test` (227 pass) and `fleet-write/dispatch.mjs --self-test` (331 pass); `check-empty-changeset.mjs --base d3f36861 --head HEAD` (exit 0); `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 31250` (exit 0, NOT governed); and `readTargetKind` / `refuseKindLabels` against the live REST objects of issue #31148 and PR #31250. No install was needed. The 32 dispatch-gates commands were not re-run; the gate record shows all 32 at exit 0.
Scope: the one file of `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main refs/seat3/pr-31250) refs/seat3/pr-31250` (merge base `d3f36861`; one commit `c9d08f393`): scripts/pm/label-write.mjs (+153 / −1). `origin/main` is now `0d0c377be`, 3 commits past the base (`30f23fef4`, `b065fad56`, `0d0c377be`, 24 files). None of them touches `scripts/pm/**` or `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/**`; SKILL.md is byte-identical at the base and on `origin/main`. Read on `origin/main` or the head: label-write.mjs (header, `refuseTwoStates`, the new kind block, `relayActions`, `parseOptions` L757-830, `rest`, `runLabelWrite` whole, `runRelease` whole, `fakeBoard` card-read, the battery ledger and floor check L1669-1690 and L2076-2095, the new battery); check-half-states.mjs (imports L969-976, `PM_EXCLUSIVE_STATE_LABELS` L6827, `GOVERNED_PR_AWAITING_MERGE_LABEL` L11472, `DECISION_INBOX_LABEL` L11479, H48 header L11384-11420); SKILL.md L100-120 and L180-205; close-cards.mjs header and its `runLabelWrite` call; fleet-write/validate.mjs and dispatch.mjs (`labels_add`, `RETIRED_LANE_REWRITE_OPS`); AGENTS.md § Writing a `--self-test`.

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs: card #31148 (body; triage 6708587186; claim 6712015904), the PR body (the same as /mnt/project-files/card-31148/body-v1.md apart from one trailing blank line), the order at /mnt/project-files/skills-seat3/order-31148.md, the gate record gates-c9d08f39.txt (32 commands, all exit 0), the commit and the net diff.

- **Item 1, the refusal.** TRUE on every path that adds labels.
  - Directions. `refuseKindLabels` refuses any of the six `PM_EXCLUSIVE_STATE_LABELS` added to a pull request, and `pm:awaiting-merge` added to an issue. It returns null for `pm:awaiting-merge` on a PR and for any state on an issue. A mixed add (a state plus `pm:awaiting-merge`) is refused on either kind, which is right: one half is always wrong.
  - Removals. `--remove` is never an input to the rule. The cleanup (`--remove needs-user-decision --add pm:awaiting-merge` on a PR) passes and reads back.
  - Placement in `runLabelWrite`. The check sits in step ②, after the targets are computed and before `route.error`, the dry-run branch, the relay pack and the direct plan. So it precedes every write: the POST, the DELETEs, the assignee calls, the relay dispatch, the PATCH fallback and step ④'s re-add. It sits before `refuseTwoStates`, and its `if` has no flag in it. `--allow-two-states` and `--dry-run` are both refused (self-test case). `--json` only changes output. `--assign` / `--unassign` / `--clear-assignees` alone add no label, so nothing is asked, which is right.
  - Placement in `runRelease`. The check sits in step ②, after the reads and before the comment file is read, before the pack and before the one relay dispatch. A release on a PR is refused with zero sends.
  - Other add paths. A grep for `label-add`, `POST`, `PATCH`, `labels_add` and `runLabelWrite` finds no third one in this file. The PATCH fallback and step ④'s re-add write only `labels.target`, which already passed the check. They can only write back a state label the PR already carried, which is the existing set and not an add by this write. The one in-process caller, close-cards.mjs, only removes.
  - Kind detection. Sound for the REST issue object. I checked it live: issue #31148 has no `pull_request` key and an `/issues/31148` URL, so it reads `issue`. PR #31250 has `pull_request` with five keys and a `/pull/31250` URL, so it reads `pull request`. Any disagreement, a null `pull_request`, or a missing object gives `kind: null` with a reason. `rest` uses `fetch`, which follows a transferred issue's redirect, so the object read is the final one. An unreadable kind refuses only an add the rule governs; `--add skip-changeset` on such a card still lands (self-test case).
  - Conventions. Exit 2 is `EXIT_USAGE`, the same as `refuseTwoStates`. The lines are `② REFUSED — …` then `⛔ NOTHING WAS WRITTEN.`, and the result carries `stoppedAt: 2` and `refusal`. `runRelease` uses its own `refuse()` with `stoppedAt: 2`, as its two-state refusal does. Each sentence names the label, the target's kind and the rule. The two sentences in the PR body are verbatim what the code prints for those inputs.
- **Item 2, the vocabulary.** TRUE. `check-half-states.mjs` on `origin/main` exports all three: `PM_EXCLUSIVE_STATE_LABELS` (L6827), `GOVERNED_PR_AWAITING_MERGE_LABEL = 'pm:awaiting-merge'` (L11472) and `DECISION_INBOX_LABEL = 'needs-user-decision'` (L11479). label-write.mjs already imported from that module on main (`PM_EXCLUSIVE_STATE_LABELS`, `PM_STATE_CLAIM`, `PM_RESIDUE_LABELS` …). The PR adds two names to the existing import, so there is no new module edge. check-half-states.mjs imports only node built-ins, `../invoked-as.mjs` and `./seat-record.mjs`; neither imports label-write.mjs, so there is no cycle. Its CLI runs behind `isEntrypoint(import.meta.url)`. Importing label-write.mjs from a scratch script printed nothing.
- **Item 3, the quoted rule text.** TRUE. On `origin/main`, SKILL.md L102 contains 「issue 上的信号」 (the 状态模型 table header), L107 contains 「只挂决策卡(issue)、⛔ 永不挂 PR」, and L194 contains 「`pm:awaiting-merge` 只挂 PR、不入六态」, each verbatim. The structural self-test case reads the file and checks all three as substrings. The 状态模型 heading the sentence names is at L100.
- **Item 4, the self-test.** TRUE.
  - Head: 163 across 13. Main: 144 across 12. The difference is 19, which is the new battery's pin.
  - The cases are meaningful. They drive the real `runLabelWrite` and `runRelease` through `driveOffline` / `driveRelease` and assert the exit, `stoppedAt`, the list of non-GET calls (empty), the relay send count (zero) and the sentence. Both directions are covered, plus all six states, `needs-user-decision`'s own line, removals on both kinds, the two passes, an unrelated add on a PR that already carries a state, the unreadable kind both ways, `readTargetKind`'s agreement table, the two flags, the relay path and the release.
  - Mutation reproduced: with both sites off, 10 fail, and they are the ten the thread lists.
  - The floor follows the file's convention and AGENTS.md § Writing a `--self-test`. The ledger pins battery names, each with its count, and `SELF_TEST_BATTERY_FLOOR` is the number of declared batteries. 12 → 13 and the new pin of 19 match what runs.
  - The fake board now answers `number`, `html_url` and `pull_request` the way GitHub's issues endpoint does, with `kind: 'issue'` by default. So every older case still reads as an issue, and all 144 still pass.
- **Item 5, real-world fallout.** No legitimate caller breaks.
  - The seat ACCEPT step (SKILL.md L189, 「同笔挂 `pm:awaiting-merge`」) and H48's remedy add `pm:awaiting-merge` to a PR. That passes.
  - Releases add `pm:queue` to an issue. That passes. `--release` is refused only on a PR, and the release already requires `pm:dispatched` plus an assignee, which a PR should never carry.
  - Every invocation of label-write in `scripts/`, `.claude/` and `.github/` was checked. The only `--add` in the docs is triage-duties.md L34, `--add pm:blocking` on cards, which the rule does not govern. close-cards.mjs calls `runLabelWrite` with removals only. fleet-token, issue-create, issue-transfer and fleet-write import only `classifyHttp`. The CI card scripts (`scheduled-full-run*.mjs`, `nightly-tiers-card.mjs`, fleet-patrols.yml) write labels through their own REST calls and never call label-write.
  - No skill or reference text puts a pm state on a PR. SKILL.md L109's "PR 则合并" is about a `Blocked-by:` target, not a label.
  - check-half-states H48 is report-only and reads labels; it writes nothing. No half-state repair path in the repo adds a state to a PR or `pm:awaiting-merge` to an issue.
- **Item 6, process.** Checked.
  - Labels are `size/m` and `skip-changeset`. No `.changeset/*` is touched. `check-empty-changeset` exits 0 (no declaring changeset added, none modified). "Check Changeset" on the head shows one success and one skipped.
  - The body has `Fixes #31148` (L4), and `Clause-②: no` (L6) and `Metadata-protocol: none` (L7), both line-initial. The 维护者速读 has six lines, in Chinese, and 「需要你做的」 names the tier. The model waiver cites the standing order of 2026-11-03 and names no model ("the project's default model").
  - No model identifier appears in the body, the diff or the commit. The trailers are `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` and `Claude-Session:`. The commit message has no card number.
  - Only the claimed file is touched (claim 6712015904: `scripts/pm/label-write.mjs`).
  - Tier: `check-governed-merges --pr 31250` exits 0. NOT governed: 0 of 1 paths hit the register, and 154 lines is under 3000. The PR is a draft with no assignees.
  - Main moved 3 commits (listed in Scope). None touches this file, check-half-states.mjs or SKILL.md.
  - Check-runs on this head, read 2026-11-07T19:55Z: 44 runs, 21 success, 20 skipped, 3 queued or in progress, 0 failed.

### ② Semver level

No changeset is right. `scripts/pm/**` is repo tooling, so no released package moves, and `skip-changeset` is the repo's path for that. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right: no spec, protocol or metadata surface changes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Claim.** The one path is inside claim 6712015904. check-half-states.mjs, docs and skills are untouched, as the claim requires. No breach.
- **Tier.** NOT governed. Ordinary queue landing after the seat's ACCEPT, as the body's 「需要你做的」 says.
- **Other label doors outside this file, confirmed for filing (see S1).**
  1. `scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs` takes a raw `labels_add` action, and `pr_create` / `issue_create` carry a `labels` list (validate.mjs L110, L1156). None of them reads the kind rule. That file already applies one rule "at the seat's door" to exactly these three ops (`RETIRED_LANE_REWRITE_OPS`), so it is the natural home for a follow-up.
  2. `scripts/ci/scheduled-full-run.mjs`, `scheduled-full-run-card.mjs`, `nightly-tiers-card.mjs` and fleet-patrols.yml add labels through their own REST calls. They target issues today, so this is low priority and is listed only for completeness.

### ④ Design judgment

- **should-fix S1: the new header says "every label reaches the board through this file", and that is not true.**
  - The relay CLI (`fleet-write/dispatch.mjs`) writes `labels_add`, and labelled `pr_create` / `issue_create`, without passing through label-write.mjs. The CI card scripts write labels with their own REST calls.
  - The incident on cloud PR #3680 shows `objectstack-fleet[bot]` as the writer. That account writes both label-write's relay stroke and a raw dispatch, so the record does not show which door was used. This PR closes label-write's door. It may not have closed the one the incident actually went through.
  - Fix in this PR: reword the sentence to what holds, for example "label-write is the label door seats are told to use, so the rule is enforced here; the relay's own adding ops are not covered yet". Then file a follow-up card for the dispatch.mjs door (③ item 1). The follow-up is outside this claim, so this PR should not add it.
- **nit N1: the match is case-sensitive.** `--add Needs-User-Decision` on a PR passes the check. GitHub label names are case-insensitive, so that spelling would probably attach the real label. `refuseTwoStates` has the same gap, so this follows the file's convention. It is a typo path, not a flag that bypasses the rule.
- **nit N2: the two call sites ask about different sets.** `runLabelWrite` asks about `options.add`, which includes a label already present. `runRelease` asks about `labels.addCalls`, which does not.
  - Effect 1: `--add pm:awaiting-merge` on an issue that already carries it is refused. That is stricter and harmless.
  - Effect 2: a release on a PR that already carries `pm:queue` beside `pm:dispatched` is not refused, even though the sentence says a release is "for issues only". The release would add nothing illegal, and the shape needs a PR that already breaks the rule twice.
  - Optional: use the same input at both sites, or say in the header why they differ.
- **nit N3: the unreadable-kind sentence has a number mismatch.** With two labels it prints "`pm:queue`, `pm:awaiting-merge` is legal on only one kind". The PR branch already switches between "is a pm card STATE" and "are pm card STATES"; the same switch would fix this.
- **nit N4: the L102 anchor is a table column header.** 「issue 上的信号」 pins the 状态模型 table's title, not a sentence. The table could be retitled while the rule stays, or the rule could change while the title stays. The other two anchors are rule sentences. This is acceptable as one of three anchors.

Verdict: PASS

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c671ea5ce560dfcc9923549aae014a54fe34c58c`
Local-runs: probe — `node scripts/pm/label-write.mjs --self-test`, run in a throwaway worktree of the head (`/tmp/claude-0/seat3/wt-31250`, since removed), because the delta adds two cases and raises the kind battery's floor (exit 0; 165 cases across 13 batteries).
Scope: delta review. One commit, `c671ea5ce` (only parent `c9d08f393`, a normal push). `git diff c9d08f393 refs/seat3/pr-31250` is one file, scripts/pm/label-write.mjs: the header sentence, `refuseKindLabels`'s unreadable-kind sentence, `runRelease`'s kind check, the battery floor and two self-test cases. Also read: the PR body v2 (stored by the seat, read back identical).

### ① Derived judgments

- **S1 is fixed.** The header no longer says every label reaches the board through this file. It now says label-write is the seat's write door, that it enforces the rule for every write it makes, and that it claims nothing about the other doors. That is true. `fleet-write/dispatch.mjs` (`labels_add`, `issue_create` / `pr_create` with labels) is the other door, and it goes to #31253.
- **N2 is fixed.** `runRelease` now asks `refuseKindLabels` about `add: [RELEASE_TO]`, the label the release adds, instead of `labels.addCalls`, the labels it would newly POST. A release on a PR that already carries `pm:queue` is now refused before the comment, with zero sends and zero direct writes. The new case pins that. The thread reports that this case alone fails against the old input. The check still sits in step ②, before the comment file is read and before the one dispatch, so the order of writes is unchanged.
- **N3 is fixed.** The unreadable-kind sentence says "is legal" for one label and "are legal" for two. One case pins both forms.
- **Floor:** the kind battery goes from 19 to 21, which matches its 21 cases. The battery count stays at 13. The head's self-test gives 165 across 13.
- **Body v2:** the counts (165, 21), the mutation figures, the line counts (+159/−1), the release bullet, the gate list (32 at `c671ea5c`, all exit 0) and the head are updated.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: repo tooling, `skip-changeset`.

### ③ Boundary flags

One file, as claimed. Nothing that landed on main since the base touches label-write.mjs, check-half-states.mjs or the pm-dispatch SKILL.md.

### ④ Design judgment

The delta does only what the first record asked for. N1 (the case-sensitive match, shared with `refuseTwoStates`) and N4 stay as they are, and N1 is carried by #31253.

Verdict: PASS
